text:
julia-cust: Hey team — after rotating our SSO service account key yesterday, our non-prod embedding requests started getting 403s. Generation calls still succeed. Any hints?

sam-cs: Hmm. Can you paste a minimal curl + response body? Also which tenant/org id and example request id if you have one?

julia-cust: Tenant: org-9254. Repro curl below (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer rbx_XXXXX' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"model":"open-1-embeddings","input":["hello world"]}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 403
{"error":"forbidden","detail":"missing_entitlements: embeddings"}

mina-eng: That payload and error text point to the token claims missing the embeddings entitlement. Generation works because the token still has `generation` in the scope set. Did you use the SSO rotation CLI or the new provisioner?

julia-cust: We used our internal rotation job which calls the SSO provider and uploads the new key via the SaaS console. It used the CLI helper `rbx-ssorotate --svcacct org-9254`. No errors in that job logs.

sam-cs: Two common pitfalls: 1) the provisioner/API expects scopes as a JSON array or space-separated string; if your job sends a CSV the provisioner might only keep the first scope. 2) There was a recent change that strips `rerank`/`embeddings` when the token is flagged as "non-interactive". Can you paste the raw token payload (JWT) we can redact? You can run `rbx token:inspect <token>` or base64-decode the middle part.

julia-cust: I decoded it — here's the claims (redacted):
```
{
  "sub":"svc-abc-123",
  "org":"org-9254",
  "scopes":"generation",   /* oops */
  "iat":1690000000
}
```

mina-eng: Yup, that confirms it. The rotation job replaced the scope string with only `generation`. If you can share the rotation invocation I can point to the line.

julia-cust: Rotation call snippet: `curl -X POST https://sso.internal/rotate -d \"svc=svc-abc-123&scopes=generation,embeddings,rerank\"` — we pass scopes as a CSV param.

sam-cs: There it is — our provisioner expects scopes as space-separated (or an array) when calling the SaaS console API. The CSV gets parsed by the intermediate service and truncated. That explains missing `embeddings`.

mina-eng: Short-term: update the rotation job to send scopes as `scopes=generation embeddings rerank` (space separated) or JSON array. We can also run a one-off re-provision to add the `embeddings` scope back for you.

julia-cust: Will change the job. Can you do the one-off re-provision while we test? It's blocking a QA pipeline.

sam-cs: Sure — escalating to provisioning team. @ops-oncall can you run a manual scope add for svc-abc-123 in org-9254? Request id cs-2839507777.

ops-oncall: On it, patching now :hammer_and_wrench:

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline started for svc-abc-123 scope-update (run-id: run_2024_11_05_12_3)

ops-oncall: Done. Token reissued with scopes: `generation embeddings rerank`. Please re-run failing request.

julia-cust: Re-run -> embedding call now returns 200 and embeddings vector. Thanks!! :tada:

mina-eng: Follow-up: after you update the rotation job please add a quick token-inspect step post-rotate to assert `embeddings` present. We can share a small script for that.

sam-cs: Marking this closed but leaving a small remediation ticket for the customer to update their job. Also logging a fix for the provisioner docs to warn about CSV vs space-separated scopes.

julia-cust: Thanks everyone, huge help.

sam-cs: Glad it's sorted. If you want, we can coordinate a backfill to re-rotate any other svc accounts created with the old job. :eyes:
